title: Ranking
idea: Brief #31. Swipe of the dentist "rates whitening trends on a scale of 1-10" TikTok: a calm guy at an office desk rating every common debloating fix with a product pop-up, fair to each (specific enemy + why it fails = the #1 pattern in 100 winning scripts), ending on ours as his favorite. New voice for our account (a man), symptom call-out on Hook 3 (the most common winning opener). Ranking format also backed by ClarityMD's top-4 ranking (68 days).

script.script:
H1, H2, H4 (same spoken line): Detox tea. Two. A lot of them are basically laxatives. You're losing water, not bloat, and you'll be living in the bathroom.
H3 (own spoken hook): If you feel bloated every day, I'm about to rank several debloating products. My favorite is the last one. Detox tea. Two. A lot of them are basically laxatives...
script.visual: Initial image (all hooks): exactly the reference's first frame: him at the desk, window behind, centred, title text on top; a generic detox tea box pops up lower centre as he says the first item.
script.on_screen_text:
H1: Rating debloating trends on a scale of 1-10 (favorite is the last one)
H2: Rating every bloating remedy women swear by, 1-10
H3: Every debloating trend ranked 1-10 (my favorite is last)
H4: No text overlay
(fixed white title at the top, like the reference)

script.script: Peppermint tea. Six. Honestly, pretty good. Cheap, calming after a big meal. Not a fix, but it's nice.
script.visual: Him at the desk; pop-up: mug of peppermint tea with a tea bag.

script.script: Apple cider vinegar shots. Three. Burns going down, rough on your teeth, and most people quit after a week.
script.visual: Pop-up: small shot glass of ACV next to a plain bottle.

script.script: Bloating pills. Four. Some help, some do nothing, and you'll end up spending a lot of money
script.visual: Pop-up: generic supplement bottle with capsules.

script.script: Cutting out foods. Five. Great if you actually have a trigger food. Miserable if you don't.
script.visual: Pop-up: plate with bread and dairy crossed out.

script.script: Laxatives. Zero. Please don't. That's not debloating, that's emptying.

A castor oil pack. Nine. And, it's my favorite.
Thousands upon thousands of women use it every day and will swear by it.
script.visual: Our real amber bottle + cotton belly wrap photo pops up (a bit bigger than the others), then the pop-up becomes a quick montage of 3 to 4 real-looking women doing the pack on the couch / in bed (wrap on, tea, relaxed).

script.script: Not only do they swear it helps bloating but also helps with liver detox, wrinkles and skin care.
script.visual: 3 fast pop-ups: wrap on a belly / roller gliding under an eye / roller on the forehead.

script.script:
43,000 people use brands called Haven and Spool.
Organic cold-pressed castor oil, hexane free. Rose quartz applicator.
roll it on your belly, wrap the cotton wrap around you and your done.
script.visual: Our bottle photo + a phone scrolling Haven & Spool 5-star reviews; macro of our label, then the rose quartz ball close-up; real-looking clip of a woman rolling it on her belly and pulling the wrap snug.

script.script: They're doing buy one, get one free right now. Click the link below.
script.visual: Two bottles + wrap photo, he points down.

editing_notes: Replicate the reference: him talking to camera at his desk the whole time (Genjitsu, motion copied from the reference 1:1). Fixed title text at the top the whole video, like the reference. For every item a square product photo pops up lower centre (same size/position as the reference) while he scores it: generic/unbranded images for the other remedies (no competitor brands or logos), our REAL product photos (Products tab) for Haven & Spool. Fast: item → score → one line, 4 to 8 s each, 60 to 75 s total. Captions like the reference (score in the caption). Claims: look/feel for us. Hooks: H1, H2, H4 = same spoken opener with different text hooks; H3 = its own spoken symptom call-out. OFFER: confirm the Complete Castor Oil Kit (oil + wrap) deal + landing page with the client before launch. Doc: Brief H+S, tab #31.

Voiceover: His own voice to camera, deadpan and quick like the reference: item, score, one honest line. Fair to every item, a little funny on the bad ones. NEEDS TO HAVE CONVICTION in their voice, it's boring to listen to a dull script. They need to speak with character.

Avatar: One man, late 30s to 40s, clean-cut, light button-up shirt, at an office desk with a big window/city view behind him, framed exactly like the reference (waist up, centred, tripod, eye level). Build EVERY shot of him in Genjitsu with the reference video as the motion reference so his movements, head tilts, hand gestures, pauses and framing copy the reference 1:1. The setting gives the authority, not a title: professional office (desk, big window, bookshelves; no framed diplomas or medical charts). NOT clearly a doctor: no white coat, scrubs, stethoscope, name badge, no 'Dr', never claims a credential.
